title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Relevant Person
tiers.description: All directors and officers of the Company (including the CEO), all direct reports of the CEO, and all other employees including consultants and contractors.

tiers.name: Connected Persons
tiers.description: A spouse or partner, child or step-child under 18, an unlisted body corporate or other entity the Relevant Person controls, a trust of which the Relevant Person is trustee and of which they or a related person is a beneficiary, or any other person over whom the Relevant Person has significant influence or control.

tiers.name: Restricted Person
tiers.description: Term used in the hedging (6.15) and margin loan (6.17) prohibitions but not itself defined anywhere in the Policy; section 2 defines only 'Relevant Person' and 'Connected Person', so this appears to be a drafting inconsistency intended to mean Relevant Person.

tiers.name: Chair of the Board
tiers.description: Distinguished only for clearance purposes: approved by the Chair of the Audit & Risk Committee, or the CEO in their absence.

tiers.name: Non-Executive Directors, Executive Directors, CEO, Chief Financial Officer, Company Secretary
tiers.description: Distinguished only for clearance purposes: approved by the Chair of the Board, or the Chair of the Audit & Risk Committee in their absence.

tiers.name: All other Relevant Persons
tiers.description: Distinguished only for clearance purposes: approved by the CEO, or the Chief Financial Officer in their absence.

definitions.hedging_definition: a transaction that operates or is intended to operate to limit the economic risk of holdings of unvested securities of the Company or vested securities of the Company which are subject to holding locks

windows.end_anchor: close of business on the day following announcement of the Company's half year financial results
close of business on the day following announcement of the Company's quarterly cash flow statement for the quarter ending 31 March
close of business on the day following announcement of the Company's full year financial results
close of business on the day following announcement of the Company's quarterly cash flow statement for the quarter ending 30 September

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board may specify 'any other period' as a Blackout Period from time to time (6.4(b)(v)); the Company Secretary notifies all Relevant Persons of these windows (6.5). The policy does not state whether such additional periods are confidential.

rules.detail: Securities is defined to include options, warrant contracts and other derivatives; the Trading Request Form expressly lists 'utilise derivatives and enter a hedging transaction' as a dealing type requiring notice and approval before trading.
rules.evidence: utilise derivatives and enter a hedging transaction

rules.detail: Absolute ban, with no clearance route, on hedging unvested Company securities.
rules.evidence: A Restricted Person must not at any time enter a transaction that operates or is intended to operate to limit the economic risk of holdings of unvested securities of the Company or vested securities of the Company which are subject to holding locks.

rules.detail: Absolute ban, with no clearance route, on hedging vested Company securities that remain subject to a holding lock.
rules.evidence: A Restricted Person must not at any time enter a transaction that operates or is intended to operate to limit the economic risk of holdings of unvested securities of the Company or vested securities of the Company which are subject to holding locks.

rules.detail: Section 6.15's express hedging ban is narrowly drawn to unvested and holding-locked securities only; hedging of fully vested, unrestricted shares is not itself named and falls back to the ordinary prior notice-and-approval requirement for any dealing.
rules.evidence: Relevant Persons are only permitted to deal in Company Securities if they have given notice and obtained approval as set out below.

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named, but a prepaid forward or similar arrangement that limits the economic risk of unvested holdings is caught by the 6.15 hedging ban.
rules.evidence: A Restricted Person must not at any time enter a transaction that operates or is intended to operate to limit the economic risk of holdings of unvested securities of the Company or vested securities of the Company which are subject to holding locks.

rules.detail: Monetisation of vested but holding-locked shares that limits economic risk is caught by the 6.15 hedging ban.
rules.evidence: A Restricted Person must not at any time enter a transaction that operates or is intended to operate to limit the economic risk of holdings of unvested securities of the Company or vested securities of the Company which are subject to holding locks.

rules.detail: A monetisation of fully vested, unrestricted shares is not caught by the narrow 6.15 hedging ban and instead falls back to the ordinary prior notice-and-approval requirement.
rules.evidence: Relevant Persons are only permitted to deal in Company Securities if they have given notice and obtained approval as set out below.

rules.detail: Short selling is not mentioned anywhere in the policy.
Securities lending is not mentioned anywhere in the policy.

CFDs are not named but fall within 'other derivatives relating to the shares' in the Securities definition and require ordinary prior clearance; a CFD used to hedge unvested or holding-locked shares would instead be caught by the 6.15 hedging ban.
rules.evidence: options to subscribe for new shares and options over existing shares, warrant contracts and other derivatives relating to the shares.

rules.detail: Absolute ban on including Company securities in a margin lending arrangement, with no clearance or exemption route named in section 6.17 itself.
rules.evidence: A Restricted Person is prohibited from including securities in the Company in a margin lending arrangement.

rules.detail: Granting security is not itself a defined dealing, but the Board assesses, case by case, the rules applicable to a Relevant Person entering into an agreement that gives a lender rights over their Company securities; margin lending specifically remains banned outright under 6.17.
rules.evidence: On a case-by-case basis the Board will assess the rules that are applicable to Relevant Persons with respect to entering into agreements that provide lenders with rights over their interests in the Company's securities.

rules.detail: Margin lending is banned outright (6.17). Other secured financing arrangements are addressed only through the Board's case-by-case assessment of agreements giving a lender rights over a Relevant Person's securities, and a resulting forced sale may (but is not automatically) be excluded from the Policy.
rules.evidence: a disposal of securities of the Company on a case-by-case basis, that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement.

rules.detail: No trading on a short-term or speculative basis; the Company defines short-term as six months or less from acquisition.
rules.evidence: Relevant Persons should not trade in Company Securities on a short-term basis or for speculative trading gain. The Company considers "short-term" to be a period of 6 months or less.

clearance.approver: Chair of the Audit & Risk Committee, or in their absence the CEO (cc Company Secretary)
clearance.post_trade_deadline: within two business days of dealing
clearance.evidence: Chair of the Board | Chair of the Audit & Risk Committee or in their absence the CEO (cc the Company Secretary).

clearance.approver: Chair of the Board, or in their absence the Chair of the Audit & Risk Committee (cc Company Secretary)
clearance.post_trade_deadline: within two business days of dealing; the Company notifies ASX on behalf of a director within five business days
clearance.evidence: Non-Executive Directors, Executive Directors, CEO, Chief Financial Officer, Company Secretary | Chair of the Board or in their absence the Chair of the Audit & Risk Committee.

clearance.approver: CEO, or in their absence the Chief Financial Officer (cc Company Secretary)
clearance.post_trade_deadline: within two business days of dealing
clearance.evidence: All other Relevant Persons | CEO or in their absence the Chief Financial Officer.

short_term.evidence: The Company considers "short-term" to be a period of 6 months or less.

exceptions.approver: Approver specified in section 7 (Chair of the Audit & Risk Committee, Chair of the Board, or CEO/CFO, depending on the person's role)
exceptions.evidence: Exceptional circumstances include severe financial hardship, compulsion by a court order or any other circumstances that are deemed exceptional.
compulsion by a court order or any other circumstances that are deemed exceptional.
trading in Company securities where trading does not result in a change of beneficial interest.
transfers of securities of the Company already held into a superannuation fund or other saving scheme in which the Relevant Person is a beneficiary.
undertakings to accept, or the acceptance of, a takeover offer.

exceptions.approver: Board (approves the plan's timing and structure)
exceptions.evidence: trading under an offer or invitation made to all or most of the security holders, such as, a rights issue, a security purchase plan, a dividend or distribution reinvestment plan and an equal access buy-back, where the plan that determines the timing and structure of the offer has been approved by the Board.

an investment in, or trading in units of, a fund or other scheme (other than a scheme only investing in the securities of the Company) where the assets of the fund or other scheme are invested at the discretion of a third party.

where a Relevant Person is a trustee, trading in the securities of the Company by that trust provided the Relevant Person is not a beneficiary of the trust and any decision to trade during a prohibited period is taken by the other trustees or by the investment managers independently of the Relevant Person.
a disposal of securities of the Company on a case-by-case basis, that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement.

the exercise (but not the sale of securities following exercise) of an option or a right under an equity incentive scheme, or the conversion of a convertible security, where the final date for the exercise of the option or right ... falls during a Blackout Period.

exemption_authority: The Approver specified in section 7 (Chair of the Audit & Risk Committee or CEO, for the Chair of the Board; Chair of the Board or Chair of the Audit & Risk Committee, for other directors/CEO/CFO/Company Secretary; CEO or CFO, for all other Relevant Persons) may grant a written waiver for exceptional circumstances (severe financial hardship, court order, or other exceptional circumstances) valid for 5 business days, given or refused without reasons and revocable if new circumstances arise; a refusal must be kept confidential by the applicant. Separately, the Board assesses case-by-case whether agreements giving a lender rights over a Relevant Person's securities (and any resulting forced sale) fall outside the Policy.

bespoke_clauses.topic: hedging ban limited to unvested/locked shares
bespoke_clauses.clause: A Restricted Person must not at any time enter a transaction that operates or is intended to operate to limit the economic risk of holdings of unvested securities of the Company or vested securities of the Company which are subject to holding locks.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The express hedging prohibition does not reach vested, unrestricted shares, so a collar over such shares is not banned outright and only needs the ordinary prior clearance under section 7, materially improving feasibility versus policies with a blanket hedging ban.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A Restricted Person is prohibited from including securities in the Company in a margin lending arrangement.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The funded collar's loan leg cannot be structured as a margin loan; it must instead be framed as a different form of secured lending to fall within the more flexible case-by-case regime in 8.1(g).

bespoke_clauses.clause: On a case-by-case basis the Board will assess the rules that are applicable to Relevant Persons with respect to entering into agreements that provide lenders with rights over their interests in the Company's securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is the most plausible route for the bank's loan and any enforcement sale, but it requires bespoke, discretionary Board sign-off rather than a pre-set clearance process, and provides no certainty of outcome.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A Restricted Person must not at any time enter a transaction ... (6.15); A Restricted Person is prohibited from including securities ... (6.17)
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Section 2 defines only 'Relevant Person' and 'Connected Person'; the undefined term 'Restricted Person' used for the hedging and margin-loan bans creates interpretive uncertainty that should be clarified with the Company Secretary before relying on any narrower reading of scope.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors should also be aware of the substantial holder provisions contained in section 671B of the Corporations Act which require certain notices to be served on the Company and the ASX when a person and their associates have a relevant interest in at least 5% of the issued voting shares in the Company and any change of more than 1% to those relevant interests occurs.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar or loan that changes a director's relevant interest by more than 1% (where holdings exceed 5%) triggers separate substantial holder notice obligations outside the Trading Policy's own clearance regime.

bespoke_clauses.clause: If a waiver is refused, the Relevant person must keep that confidential.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: If clearance for the collar is refused under the exceptional-circumstances process, the executive cannot disclose that refusal, limiting the ability to renegotiate timing openly with the bank.

bespoke_clauses.clause: If approval to deal in the Company's securities is granted, the dealing must be conducted within five business days from the date of approval (or such other period of time as specified by the Approver). If the Relevant Person does not deal in securities within this time period, the approval will lapse.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The put/call trade and loan drawdown must be completed within 5 business days of approval (unless the Approver extends this), or fresh clearance must be obtained.

summary: A funded collar over vested, unrestricted Vitrafy shares is plausible, because the express hedging ban in section 6.15 is narrowly drawn to unvested securities and vested securities subject to a holding lock - it does not reach vested shares free of any lock, which instead only need the ordinary prior notice-and-approval process under section 7 (Chair of the Audit & Risk Committee, Chair of the Board, or CEO/CFO, depending on the person's role). The loan leg cannot be structured as a margin loan, since section 6.17 bans margin lending arrangements over Company securities outright with no exemption; however, other secured lending arrangements granting a lender rights over the executive's shares are assessed by the Board case-by-case under section 8.1(g), and a resulting forced sale may be carved out of the Policy if the Board agrees. Both legs must otherwise sit outside the quarterly, half-year and full-year blackout periods (or be approved under the 5-business-day exceptional-circumstances waiver for hardship or court order), be executed within 5 business days of clearance, and be reported to the Company Secretary within 2 business days of dealing. The undefined term 'Restricted Person' used in the hedging and margin-loan clauses, and the discretionary, case-by-case nature of the secured-lending carve-out, leave structuring risk that should be cleared with the Board or Company Secretary before executing the bank's loan documentation.
